nodes.summary: There is a convergent sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers that cannot be written as $z_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k y_{n-k}$ for all $n \ge 0$ with convergent sequences $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers. That is, the claim of Scottish Book Problem 8 is false.
nodes.title: Mazur's Problem 8 has a negative answer

nodes.summary: This is the statement, asked about in form (b) of Mazur's Problem 8 in the Scottish Book typescript, that every convergent sequence $(z_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers can be written as $z_n = \frac{1}{n+1} \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k y_{n-k}$ for all $n \ge 0$, where $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ are convergent sequences of real numbers.
